citations.quote:
A **multitensor category over $k$** is a locally finite $k$-linear abelian,
rigid monoidal category whose tensor product is $k$-bilinear in both variables.
A **tensor category** is a multitensor category for which
$\operatorname{End}(\mathbf1)\cong k$ as $k$-algebras.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category and let $X$ be an object of
$\mathcal C$. Each **formal canonical composite** on $X^{\otimes n}$ built
from associators, unitors, braidings, and their inverses has an underlying
braid in $B_n$. If two such formal composites have equal underlying braids,
then their interpreted morphisms in $\mathcal C$ are equal. Different formal
braids may, of course, have the same interpretation in a particular braided
category.

For $n\ge2$, the **braid group** $B_n$ is the group with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and relations

$$\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\qquad(1\le i\le n-2),$$

$$\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\qquad(1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Equivalently,

$$B_n=\langle \sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\ \sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\ (1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

interpreted in the sense of [[def-group-presentation]] and
[[def-relators-relations-and-finite-presentations]].

For $n=0$ and $n=1$, there are no generators, and $B_n$ is the trivial group
given by the empty presentation.

Let $\langle X\mid R\rangle$ be a presentation, let $H$ be a group, and let
$u:X\to H$ be a function. If the evaluation of every $r\in R$ under $u$ is
$e_H$, then there is a unique homomorphism

$$\overline u:\langle X\mid R\rangle\longrightarrow H$$

with $\overline u([x])=u(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Moreover, $\overline u$ is
surjective if and only if $u(X)$ generates $H$.

Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field with bijective antipode, and let $(h_i)$ and $(f_i)$ be dual bases of $H$ and $H^*$. In the factor order $D(H)=H^{*\mathrm{op}}\otimes H$, the tensor

$$R=\sum_i(f_i\otimes1_H)\otimes(\varepsilon_H\otimes h_i)$$

is basis-independent and invertible, with

$$R^{-1}=\sum_i(f_i\otimes1_H)\otimes(\varepsilon_H\otimes S^{-1}(h_i)).$$

It is quasitriangular in the convention

$$R\Delta_D(d)=\Delta_D^{\mathrm{op}}(d)R,\qquad(\Delta_D\otimes\operatorname{id})R=R_{13}R_{23},\qquad\alpha^{-1}_{D,D,D}(\operatorname{id}\otimes\Delta_D)R=R_{13}R_{12}.$$

On every pair of left $D(H)$-modules, $\tau\circ R$ is the Yetter–Drinfeld braiding of [[thm-hh-double-modules-and-yetter-drinfeld-modules]].

derivations.claim: By the canonical rebracketing property in [F3], there is a canonical isomorphism $\rho_{n,i}:P_n(X)\to Q_{n,i}(X)$ built from the associators and unitors; every factor is invertible, so the composite is invertible. The map $\operatorname{id}\otimes c_{X,X}\otimes\operatorname{id}$ is an endomorphism of $Q_{n,i}(X)$, because $c_{X,X}$ is an isomorphism from $X\otimes X$ to the same ordered object $X\otimes X$. Conjugating gives the displayed endomorphism $B_i^X$ of $P_n(X)$.

If $\rho_{n,i}$ and $\rho'_{n,i}$ are two such canonical rebracketings, then $\rho'_{n,i}\rho_{n,i}^{-1}$ has trivial underlying braid. Inserting the same local $c_{X,X}$ gives formal composites with underlying braid $\sigma_i$; [F3] makes the resulting endomorphisms equal. Thus $B_i^X$ is independent of the rebracketing path.

The two composites $B_i^XB_{i+1}^XB_i^X$ and $B_{i+1}^XB_i^XB_{i+1}^X$ have underlying braid words $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i$ and $\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$, equal in $B_n$; operators with $|i-j|>1$ have the equal underlying words $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i$. By [F3] the corresponding morphisms are equal.

Each $B_i^X$ is invertible by step 1.1 and [F2]. The relations in step 3.1 therefore satisfy the Artin presentation [F4], and [F5] gives the unique homomorphism $\varrho_n:B_n\to\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal C}(P_n(X))$ with $\varrho_n(\sigma_i)=B_i^X$.

In the Hopf-module convention, the coproduct supplies the tensor-product module action, while [F6]'s intertwining identity $R\Delta_D(d)=\Delta_D^{\mathrm{op}}(d)R$ makes $\tau\circ R$ the exchange braiding; [F6] fixes the factor order $H^{*\mathrm{op}}\otimes H$. This supplies the category braiding only when the relevant module objects and category structure are supplied. No semisimplicity, unitarity, modularity, or physical realization follows from [F6] alone.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$, so it is finite semisimple, rigid, monoidal, and has simple unit [[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects and let $n\ge0$. Fix one representative of each simple isomorphism class for the internal path labels; the external objects $a,b,c$ need not equal their representatives. Set $T_0=b$ and recursively fix the left-associated parenthesization $T_{j+1}:=T_j\otimes a$. The **fixed-boundary anyonic path space** is

$$H_{a,n;b,c}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,T_n).$$

For simple labels $x,y$, define the split multiplicity space $W_{x,a}^y:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(y,x\otimes a)$. For $n\ge1$, a fusion path is a sequence of simple labels $x_0=b,x_1,\ldots,x_n=c$, with $x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}$ drawn from the fixed representative set, together with, for every $1\le j\le n$, one basis index $\mu_j$ in a chosen basis $B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$ of $W_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$. The basis index is retained even when distinct indices have the same adjacent labels. Fusion rules are the nonnegative integers $N_{x a}^{y}$ in $[x][a]=\sum_yN_{x a}^{y}[y]$ [[def-fusion-rules]].

For $n=0$, there is no path if $b\not\cong c$. If $b\cong c$, fix an isomorphism $u_{c,b}:c\to b$ and take it as the single empty-path vector (use $u_{b,b}=\operatorname{id}_b$ when the objects coincide). In the unitary setting choose this isomorphism unitary.

For $n\ge1$, if $i_j\in B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$ is the selected inclusion $x_j\to x_{j-1}\otimes a$, define the path composite by $\gamma_0:=\operatorname{id}_b$ and $\gamma_j:=(\gamma_{j-1}\otimes\operatorname{id}_a)\circ i_j:x_j\to T_j$. For $x_n=c$, $\gamma_n$ is a vector in $H_{a,n;b,c}$. The next lemma proves these composites form a basis and computes the dimension. No Hilbert-space or physical Hamiltonian structure is part of this definition.

Fix a fusion-path space with repeated simple site charge $a$, a position $i$ with two adjacent $a$-labels, and a simple output $s$ of $a\otimes a$, chosen from the fixed internal representative set of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. Choose bases in the split spaces $\operatorname{Hom}(z,x\otimes y)$ at every vertex of the trees used below, retaining the fixed path vertex bases on the fixed tree. In the tree basis where this adjacent pair is fused first, let $\Pi_s$ be the projection onto the direct summand with pair output $s$, acting as the identity on every multiplicity index inside that channel and as zero on all other pair outputs. Let $A_i:T_{\mathrm{fixed}}\to T_{\mathrm{pair}}$ be a typed composite of associators and their inverses carrying the fixed path tree to this pair-first tree, without permuting the ordered inputs (including the boundary charge). In the split-tree bases of $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, let $F_i$ be the matrix of $h\mapsto A_i\circ h$, with target coordinates as rows and source coordinates as columns. The proof below constructs these bases and proves invertibility in any complex fusion category. Define the **local channel projector** in the fixed path basis by

$$P_{i,s}:=F_i^{-1}\Pi_sF_i.$$

This is an idempotent for any fusion category because $F_i$ is invertible. In a unitary fusion category with orthonormal tree bases, $F_i$ is unitary and $P_{i,s}$ is an orthogonal projection. The channel projection includes every multiplicity coordinate; the definition has no multiplicity-free restriction. The split Hom convention here is $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, as in [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. In the unitary case with adjoint vertex bases, each local left-to-right split recoupling matrix is the entrywise conjugate of the QC25 inverse-precomposition F matrix, as proved below; they agree for the displayed real Fibonacci and Ising blocks.

Let $a,b,c,d$ be simple charges in a unitary fusion category, and put
$P_L=((a\otimes b)\otimes c)$ and $P_R=a\otimes(b\otimes c)$. The local
fusion-tree basis result [[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]] identifies

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_e V_{ab}^e\otimes V_{ec}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d),$$

and

$$\mathcal H_R:=\bigoplus_f V_{bc}^f\otimes V_{af}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_R,d),$$

by the corresponding tree compositions. These direct sums carry the
orthonormal left- and right-tree bases. If $\mu:a\otimes b\to e$ and
$\nu:e\otimes c\to d$ are vertex basis maps, write
$L_{e,\mu,\nu}:=\nu\circ(\mu\otimes\operatorname{id}_c):P_L\to d$. If
$\rho:b\otimes c\to f$ and $\sigma:a\otimes f\to d$ are vertex basis maps,
write $R_{f,\rho,\sigma}:=\sigma\circ(\operatorname{id}_a\otimes\rho):P_R\to d$.
Let $\alpha_{a,b,c}:P_L\to P_R$ be the associator. Define the **F-symbol
matrix** $F_d^{abc}$ by

$$L_{e,\mu,\nu}\circ\alpha_{a,b,c}^{-1} =\sum_{f,\rho,\sigma}F_d^{abc}[(f,\rho,\sigma),(e,\mu,\nu)]R_{f,\rho,\sigma}.$$

Rows index target-tree labels and multiplicity indices; columns index
source-tree labels and multiplicity indices. The sums retain every fusion
channel and every multiplicity coordinate.
If the fixed-total fusion space is zero-dimensional, the F-symbol is the unique
empty $0\times0$ matrix.

Let $b,c,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be simple objects of a unitary fusion category, with $n\ge2$, and let $T_{\mathrm{fixed}}$ be a fixed parenthesization of $b\otimes a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n$. Equip $H=\operatorname{Hom}(c,T_{\mathrm{fixed}})$ with the split Hom inner product $g^\dagger h=\langle h,g\rangle\operatorname{id}_c$ and choose orthonormal split vertex bases in the trees below. Fix $1\le i<n$. Let $A_i:T_{\mathrm{fixed}}\to T_{\mathrm{pair}}$ be a composite of associators and inverses to a tree fusing $a_i,a_{i+1}$ first, without permuting inputs. Let $F_i$ be the matrix of $h\mapsto A_i\circ h$, with target rows and source columns, and let $\Pi_s$ project onto all pair-first coordinates of simple pair output $s$, retaining every multiplicity index. Define $P_{i,s}:=F_i^{-1}\Pi_sF_i$, extending the repeated-charge construction of [[def-anyonic-local-channel-projector]] to these arbitrary simple site charges. Then $(P_{i,s})_s$ is pairwise orthogonal, self-adjoint, and idempotent, and its sum over all simple outputs of $a_i\otimes a_{i+1}$ is the identity on $H$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary spherical fusion category over $\mathbb C$, with pivotal structure and spherical dimension as in [[def-pivotal-structure]], [[def-spherical-structure]], and [[def-the-dimension-of-an-object-relative-to-a-pivotal-structure]]. Let $a$ be a self-dual simple object with $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$. Choose a unit vector $v:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ spanning the one-dimensional vacuum split space and let $d_a>0$ be its positive spherical dimension.

A **normalized vacuum-channel self-duality datum** is a supplied pair of maps $\operatorname{coev}:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ and $\operatorname{ev}:a\otimes a\to\mathbf1$ of the form

$$\operatorname{coev}=\sqrt{d_a}\,v,\qquad \operatorname{ev}=\kappa_a\sqrt{d_a}\,v^\dagger,$$

where $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$ and the two duality zig-zag identities hold after the self-duality identification, using the left-dual convention of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]. We call $\kappa_a$ the **Frobenius–Schur sign in this normalized cup/cap convention**. It is not a braiding or $R$-symbol phase.

This item records supplied normalized duality data; it does not assert that every self-dual simple object admits the displayed gauge or prove a trace, ribbon, or category-equivalence theorem. An example must supply the datum or compute the sign from coherent normalized F-data; fusion rules alone do not specify it.

Let $a$ and $(v,\operatorname{ev},\operatorname{coev},d_a,\kappa_a)$ be as in [[def-anyonic-frobenius-schur-sign]]. In the multiplicity-free vacuum-normalized gauge of [[def-qc-tqc-f-symbol]],

$$\left(F^{aaa}_a\right)_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}=\frac{\kappa_a}{d_a},\qquad \delta_a:=\frac{1}{\left((F^{aaa}_a)^{-1}\right)_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}}=\kappa_a d_a.$$

For fixed ordered tensor inputs and fixed source and target parenthesizations, any two sequences of canonical associator F-moves between them induce the same coordinate map. Consequently, conjugating a fixed pair-channel projection by either sequence gives the same operator on the fusion-path space.

derivations.claim: Choose a parenthesization grouping the three sites $a_i,a_{i+1},a_{i+2}$ and decompose the split-tree basis by their simple total charge $y$ and the spectator labels. If the first pair fuses to $\mathbf1$, then its fusion with the third $a$ has total charge $y=\mathbf1\otimes a\cong a$; the same is true if the last pair fuses to $\mathbf1$. On the $y=a$ block each vacuum-channel subspace has dimension $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}N_{\mathbf1 a}^{a}=1$, since $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$ and the tensor unit acts as the identity. On every $y\not\cong a$ block both projectors vanish. Each fixed spectator label and multiplicity coordinate gives a copy of this local block, where $P_i$ and $P_{i+1}$ act as rank-one orthogonal projections onto unit vectors $e$ and $f$, by [F4].

By the F-symbol coordinate convention in [F3], the vacuum-to-vacuum entry of the three-site F-move is the coordinate of one unit basis vector in the other tree basis. Therefore $|\langle e,f\rangle|=|(F^{aaa}_a)_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}|=|\kappa_a/d_a|=1/d_a$ by [F5] and [F6], so $|\langle e,f\rangle|^2=d_a^{-2}$.

For unit vectors $e,f$, the rank-one projection formula gives $P_fP_eP_f=|\langle e,f\rangle|^2P_f$: on $x$, its value is $\langle f,x\rangle\langle e,f\rangle\langle f,e\rangle f$. Therefore $P_{i+1}P_iP_{i+1}=d_a^{-2}P_{i+1}$ on each $y=a$ spectator copy; on every other block both sides are zero. Tensoring with the spectator identities and transporting to the fixed path parenthesization preserves the relation by [F7].

Since $\delta_a=\kappa_ad_a$ and $\kappa_a^2=1$, $\delta_a^2=d_a^2$. Thus $U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=\delta_a^3P_{i+1}P_iP_{i+1}=\delta_a^3d_a^{-2}P_{i+1}=\delta_aP_{i+1}=U_{i+1}$. The sign is retained in the final equality.

finite_checks.calculation: For unit vectors e,f spanning the two vacuum-channel lines, |<e,f>|²=|κ_a/d_a|²=d_a^{-2}; hence P_{i+1}P_iP_{i+1}=d_a^{-2}P_{i+1} and δ_a³d_a^{-2}P_{i+1}=δ_aP_{i+1}.
finite_checks.disposition: This finite-dimensional block calculation is the complete local relation; all spectator blocks are copies or zero.

boundaries.reason: The lemma fixes n≥3 and an adjacent pair of pair-projector indices.

boundaries.evidence: On a zero path block or a triple block whose total charge is not a, both local vacuum projectors vanish; steps 1.1 and 3.1 give 0=0.
The vacuum fusion multiplicity N_aa^1=1 and unit fusion N_1a^a=1 make each local vacuum-channel subspace rank one on the total-a block by step 1.1.
The supplied d_a is positive and κ_a=±1, so δ_a²=d_a²>0; step 4.1 uses this exact normalization.
The allowed range 1≤i≤n−2 is stated explicitly and step 1.1 groups precisely those three sites.

boundaries.reason: A fixed parenthesization and finite split-tree basis are given; the proof requires no nonempty selection.
The claim is a one-way adjacent relation, not an iff.
No converse construction from Temperley–Lieb relations to fusion data is claimed.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary spherical fusion category over $\mathbb C$. Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects, with $a$ self-dual, $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$, and supply the normalized vacuum-channel self-duality datum with sign $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$ and positive spherical dimension $d_a$. For $n\ge3$, take the fixed-boundary repeated-$a$ path space $H_{a,n;b,c}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,T_n)$ with $T_0=b$ and $T_{j+1}=T_j\otimes a$, as in [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. Let $P_i=P_{i,\mathbf1}$ be the orthogonal local vacuum-channel projectors and put $U_i=\delta_aP_i$, where $\delta_a=\kappa_ad_a$. Then, for every $1\le i\le n-2$,

$$U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=U_{i+1}.$$

This supplies the reverse adjacent relation for the repeated-charge Temperley–Lieb family.

Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, with $S_0=\{1\}$ as in
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]. Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one
indeterminate $v$ over $\mathbb Z$. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke
algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1),$$
that is, the quotient of the free unital associative $A$-algebra on
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these relators. The
first relation is written in the **RG-13 quadratic normalization**
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, equivalent to the displayed form over $A$. For $n\le1$ there
are no generators and we set $H_v(n):=A$.

**Standard basis elements.** Let $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ with
simple transpositions $s_i=(i\ i+1)$
([[def-symmetric-group]]), and let $w\in S_n$ have inversion length $\ell(w)=\ell$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]). Choose a reduced expression
$w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$, that is, a word of the minimal length $\ell(w)$
representing $w$, and put
$$T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\in H_v(n),$$
the empty product when $w$ is the identity of $S_n$, so that $T_w=1$ for that
element. That $T_w$ is independent of the chosen reduced expression, and that
the elements $T_w$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, is proved in the
standard-basis theorem below
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); the notation
distinguishes the generator $T_i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ from $T_w$ for the group
element $w$.

**Specializations.** Let $R$ be a commutative $A$-algebra with structure map
$\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0$, and suppose $v_0\in R^\times$. The
**specialization** of $H_v(n)$ at $v_0$ is the $R$-algebra
$R\otimes_AH_v(n)$; it is presented over $R$ by the images of $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
subject to the same relations with $v$ replaced by $v_0$, and we write $H_{v_0}(n)$
for it. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$, where the
quadratic relation becomes $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation
relations, and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining
$\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$; the latter specializes the generic algebra to
the Hecke algebra attached to the finite general linear group. The condition
$v_0\in R^\times$ is part of the definition of a specialization and, for a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, excludes $v_0=0$. The zero ring
is allowed: its unique element is a unit and its specialization is the zero algebra.

Let $H(n)$ be the Hecke tower over $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]$ of
[[def-markov-trace-on-the-type-a-hecke-tower]]. Then: (1) the elements
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ are units of $H(n)$ with
$T_i^{-1}=v^{-1}T_i+(v^{-1}-1)$; (2) the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto T_i$
descends to a group homomorphism
$$\pi_n:B_n\longrightarrow H(n)^{\times},\qquad \pi_n(\sigma_i)=T_i,$$
where $H(n)^{\times}$ is the group of units of $H(n)$; (3) for every Artin word
$\beta=\sigma_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$ one has
$\pi_n(\beta)=T_{i_1}^{\varepsilon_1}\cdots T_{i_k}^{\varepsilon_k}$, and
$\pi_{n+1}(\iota_n^{\mathrm{Br}}(\beta))=\iota_n(\pi_n(\beta))$ for all
$\beta\in B_n$ under the standard inclusion of braid groups $B_n\to B_{n+1}$.

For $n\ge2$, the **braid group** $B_n$ is the group with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and relations

$$\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\qquad(1\le i\le n-2),$$

$$\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\qquad(1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1).$$

Equivalently,

$$B_n=\langle \sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\ (1\le i\le n-2),\ \sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i\ (1\le i,j\le n-1,\ |i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

interpreted in the sense of [[def-group-presentation]] and
[[def-relators-relations-and-finite-presentations]].

For $n=0$ and $n=1$, there are no generators, and $B_n$ is the trivial group
given by the empty presentation.

Let $\langle X\mid R\rangle$ be a presentation, let $H$ be a group, and let
$u:X\to H$ be a function. If the evaluation of every $r\in R$ under $u$ is
$e_H$, then there is a unique homomorphism

$$\overline u:\langle X\mid R\rangle\longrightarrow H$$

with $\overline u([x])=u(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Moreover, $\overline u$ is
surjective if and only if $u(X)$ generates $H$.

derivations.claim: Since $U_i^2=\delta U_i$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, $(qI_V-U_i)(q^{-1}I_V-U_i)=I_V-(q+q^{-1})U_i+U_i^2=I_V$. The product in the reverse order is the same polynomial in $U_i$, so $B_i^{-1}=q^{-1}I_V-U_i$.

For adjacent $i,i+1$, expansion and the square and adjacent Temperley–Lieb relations give $(qI_V-U_i)(qI_V-U_{i+1})(qI_V-U_i)-(qI_V-U_{i+1})(qI_V-U_i)(qI_V-U_{i+1})=-(q^2-q\delta+1)(U_i-U_{i+1})=0$, since $q\delta=q^2+1$. Thus the adjacent braid relation holds.
We have $B_i-qI_V=-U_i$ and $B_i+q^{-1}I_V=\delta I_V-U_i$; hence $(B_i-qI_V)(B_i+q^{-1}I_V)=-\delta U_i+U_i^2=0$.
If $|i-j|>1$, then $B_iB_j-B_jB_i=U_iU_j-U_jU_i=0$. Together with step 1.1, the $B_i$ are units satisfying all relators of [F5].
By [F6] applied to [F5] and the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto B_i$, step 2.2 supplies a unique homomorphism $\rho_n:B_n\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ with $\rho_n(\sigma_i)=B_i$.

Let $\widetilde T_i:=qB_i$. They satisfy the braid and distant relations by steps 1.2–2.2, and $(\widetilde T_i-q^2I_V)(\widetilde T_i+I_V)=q^2(B_i-qI_V)(B_i+q^{-1}I_V)=0$. Consequently the generator map from the free unital algebra kills every defining relator of $H_{q^2}(n)$, so its defining ideal lies in the kernel and the map factors through the quotient $H_{q^2}(n)$. This gives the stated unital Hecke-algebra representation.

Apply the coefficient map $\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1},z]\to\mathbb C$, $v\mapsto q^2$, $z\mapsto0$, to the Hecke tower in [F4]. By its defining scalar-extension construction and the specialization in [F3], the resulting algebra is $H_{q^2}(n)$; base change carries [F4]'s braid homomorphism to $\eta_n:B_n\to H_{q^2}(n)^\times$ with $\eta_n(\sigma_i)=T_i$. Composing with $\Phi_n$ from step 3.2 sends $\sigma_i$ to $qB_i$, identifying the chosen normalization against the standard Hecke generator assignment. No Markov trace or link-invariant claim is used.

If $V$ is a complex Hilbert space, $U_i$ is bounded self-adjoint, and $|q|=1$, then $B_i^*=\overline q I_V-U_i=q^{-1}I_V-U_i=B_i^{-1}$ by step 1.1, so $B_i$ is unitary. For the repeated-$a$ anyonic path family, [F1] and [F2] supply both adjacent relations, the square relation, and distant commutation with the signed $\delta_a=\kappa_ad_a$; whenever $q+q^{-1}=\delta_a$, it therefore meets the operator hypotheses of this theorem. No sign is replaced by $+1$.

Let $n\ge2$, let $V$ be a complex vector space, and let $U_1,\ldots,U_{n-1}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$. Suppose $\delta\in\mathbb C$, $q\in\mathbb C^\times$, and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, and assume

$$U_i^2=\delta U_i,\qquad U_iU_{i+1}U_i=U_i,\qquad U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=U_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad U_iU_j=U_jU_i\quad(|i-j|>1).$$

Define $B_i:=qI_V-U_i$. Then each $B_i$ is invertible with $B_i^{-1}=q^{-1}I_V-U_i$; the $B_i$ satisfy the Artin braid and far-commutation relations; and

$$(B_i-qI_V)(B_i+q^{-1}I_V)=0.$$

Thus $\sigma_i\mapsto B_i$ defines a group homomorphism $B_n\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. If $H_v(n)$ is the generic type-A Hecke algebra with $(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, its scalar specialization $H_{q^2}(n)$ has a unital algebra representation $T_i\mapsto qB_i$. This is the standard Hecke normalization because $(qB_i-q^2I_V)(qB_i+I_V)=0$. If $V$ is a complex Hilbert space and each $U_i$ is bounded self-adjoint, then $\delta\in\mathbb R$ and $|q|=1$ imply that each $B_i$ is unitary. No faithfulness, diagonalizability, or physical realization is asserted.

Let $n\ge0$ be an integer, with $S_0=\{1\}$ as in
[[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]. Let $A:=\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]$ be the ring of Laurent polynomials in one
indeterminate $v$ over $\mathbb Z$. For $n\ge2$ the **generic type-A Hecke
algebra** $H_v(n)$ is the associative unital $A$-algebra presented by generators
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ and the relations
$$T_i^2=(v-1)T_i+v\quad(1\le i<n),\qquad T_iT_{i+1}T_i=T_{i+1}T_iT_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad T_iT_j=T_jT_i\quad(1\le i,j<n,\ |i-j|>1),$$
that is, the quotient of the free unital associative $A$-algebra on
$T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$ by the two-sided ideal generated by these relators. The
first relation is written in the **RG-13 quadratic normalization**
$(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, equivalent to the displayed form over $A$. For $n\le1$ there
are no generators and we set $H_v(n):=A$.

**Standard basis elements.** Let $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\dots,n\})$ with
simple transpositions $s_i=(i\ i+1)$
([[def-symmetric-group]]), and let $w\in S_n$ have inversion length $\ell(w)=\ell$
([[def-weyl-group-and-length-for-finite-gl-n]]). Choose a reduced expression
$w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_\ell}$, that is, a word of the minimal length $\ell(w)$
representing $w$, and put
$$T_w:=T_{i_1}\cdots T_{i_\ell}\in H_v(n),$$
the empty product when $w$ is the identity of $S_n$, so that $T_w=1$ for that
element. That $T_w$ is independent of the chosen reduced expression, and that
the elements $T_w$ form an $A$-basis of $H_v(n)$, is proved in the
standard-basis theorem below
([[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]); the notation
distinguishes the generator $T_i$ with $1\le i\le n-1$ from $T_w$ for the group
element $w$.

**Specializations.** Let $R$ be a commutative $A$-algebra with structure map
$\mathbb Z[v^{\pm1}]\to R$, $v\mapsto v_0$, and suppose $v_0\in R^\times$. The
**specialization** of $H_v(n)$ at $v_0$ is the $R$-algebra
$R\otimes_AH_v(n)$; it is presented over $R$ by the images of $T_1,\dots,T_{n-1}$
subject to the same relations with $v$ replaced by $v_0$, and we write $H_{v_0}(n)$
for it. Two specializations are used on this page: $v\mapsto1$, where the
quadratic relation becomes $T_i^2=1$ together with the braid and commutation
relations, and $v\mapsto q$, where $q$ is the prime power defining
$\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb F_q)$; the latter specializes the generic algebra to
the Hecke algebra attached to the finite general linear group. The condition
$v_0\in R^\times$ is part of the definition of a specialization and, for a nonzero coefficient ring $R$, excludes $v_0=0$. The zero ring
is allowed: its unique element is a unit and its specialization is the zero algebra.

For $n\ge2$, the symmetric group $S_n$ has the presentation

$$S_n=\langle s_1,\dots,s_{n-1}\mid s_i^2=1,\ s_is_{i+1}s_i=s_{i+1}s_is_{i+1},\ s_is_j=s_js_i\ (|i-j|>1)\rangle,$$

where, after relabelling the underlying set $n=\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ as
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$, $s_i$ corresponds to the adjacent transposition
$(i\ i+1)$. For
$n=0,1$, the trivial group has the empty presentation.

For $n\ge2$, use the one-based model $S_n^{(1)}:=\operatorname{Sym}(\{1,\ldots,n\})$, identified with the library's $S_n=\operatorname{Sym}(\{0,\ldots,n-1\})$ by conjugation with $\kappa_n(k)=k+1$ ([[def-finite-symmetric-group-and-permutation-notation]], [[thm-adjacent-transpositions-generate-the-symmetric-group]]). Write $S_n$ in this transported model below. The assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto(i\ i+1)$ extends to a surjective homomorphism

$$\pi_n:B_n\longrightarrow S_n.$$

In the library's zero-based model, the same map is $\sigma_i\mapsto(i-1\ i)$, obtained by conjugating $\pi_n$ with $\kappa_n^{-1}$.

Let $\langle X\mid R\rangle$ be a presentation, let $H$ be a group, and let
$u:X\to H$ be a function. If the evaluation of every $r\in R$ under $u$ is
$e_H$, then there is a unique homomorphism

$$\overline u:\langle X\mid R\rangle\longrightarrow H$$

with $\overline u([x])=u(x)$ for every $x\in X$. Moreover, $\overline u$ is
surjective if and only if $u(X)$ generates $H$.

derivations.claim: At $q=1$, the parameter relation gives $\delta=2$. For every $i$, $B_i^2=(I_V-U_i)^2=I_V-2U_i+U_i^2=I_V$, using $U_i^2=2U_i$ from [F1].

The general quadratic in [F1] factors as $(B_i-qI_V)(B_i+q^{-1}I_V)=0$, whose scalar roots are $q$ and $-q^{-1}$; equality of those roots is equivalent to $q^2=-1$. This polynomial relation alone asserts no diagonalization.

By [F1], the $B_i$ also satisfy the adjacent braid and distant-commutation relators. Along with step 1.1, these are exactly the Coxeter relators in [F3], so [F5] gives a homomorphism $\widetilde\rho_n:S_n\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ with $\widetilde\rho_n(s_i)=B_i$.

The composite $\widetilde\rho_n\circ\pi_n$, with $\pi_n$ from [F4], and the braid representation $\rho_n$ from [F1] agree on every generator $\sigma_i$, since both send it to $B_i$. The generators determine a homomorphism from $B_n$, so $\rho_n=\widetilde\rho_n\circ\pi_n$.

The Hecke representation of the preceding theorem sends $T_i$ to $qB_i$, which equals $B_i$ at $q=1$. The generic relation $(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$ in [F2] then becomes $T_i^2=I_V$; together with the braid and distant relations these are exactly the Coxeter generator relations in [F3]. Thus the specialized Hecke generators act by the same generator assignment as $\widetilde\rho_n$.

To see that involutivity is not forced for general $q$, take $V=\mathbb C$, $U_i=0$ for every $i$, $q=2$, and $\delta=5/2$. All Temperley–Lieb relations hold, while $B_i=2I_V$ and $B_i^2=4I_V\ne I_V$.

Fix a fusion-path space with repeated simple site charge $a$, a position $i$ with two adjacent $a$-labels, and a simple output $s$ of $a\otimes a$, chosen from the fixed internal representative set of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. Choose bases in the split spaces $\operatorname{Hom}(z,x\otimes y)$ at every vertex of the trees used below, retaining the fixed path vertex bases on the fixed tree. In the tree basis where this adjacent pair is fused first, let $\Pi_s$ be the projection onto the direct summand with pair output $s$, acting as the identity on every multiplicity index inside that channel and as zero on all other pair outputs. Let $A_i:T_{\mathrm{fixed}}\to T_{\mathrm{pair}}$ be a typed composite of associators and their inverses carrying the fixed path tree to this pair-first tree, without permuting the ordered inputs (including the boundary charge). In the split-tree bases of $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, let $F_i$ be the matrix of $h\mapsto A_i\circ h$, with target coordinates as rows and source coordinates as columns. The proof below constructs these bases and proves invertibility in any complex fusion category. Define the **local channel projector** in the fixed path basis by

$$P_{i,s}:=F_i^{-1}\Pi_sF_i.$$

This is an idempotent for any fusion category because $F_i$ is invertible. In a unitary fusion category with orthonormal tree bases, $F_i$ is unitary and $P_{i,s}$ is an orthogonal projection. The channel projection includes every multiplicity coordinate; the definition has no multiplicity-free restriction. The split Hom convention here is $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, as in [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. In the unitary case with adjoint vertex bases, each local left-to-right split recoupling matrix is the entrywise conjugate of the QC25 inverse-precomposition F matrix, as proved below; they agree for the displayed real Fibonacci and Ising blocks.

Let $b,c,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be simple objects of a unitary fusion category, with $n\ge2$, and let $T_{\mathrm{fixed}}$ be a fixed parenthesization of $b\otimes a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_n$. Equip $H=\operatorname{Hom}(c,T_{\mathrm{fixed}})$ with the split Hom inner product $g^\dagger h=\langle h,g\rangle\operatorname{id}_c$ and choose orthonormal split vertex bases in the trees below. Fix $1\le i<n$. Let $A_i:T_{\mathrm{fixed}}\to T_{\mathrm{pair}}$ be a composite of associators and inverses to a tree fusing $a_i,a_{i+1}$ first, without permuting inputs. Let $F_i$ be the matrix of $h\mapsto A_i\circ h$, with target rows and source columns, and let $\Pi_s$ project onto all pair-first coordinates of simple pair output $s$, retaining every multiplicity index. Define $P_{i,s}:=F_i^{-1}\Pi_sF_i$, extending the repeated-charge construction of [[def-anyonic-local-channel-projector]] to these arbitrary simple site charges. Then $(P_{i,s})_s$ is pairwise orthogonal, self-adjoint, and idempotent, and its sum over all simple outputs of $a_i\otimes a_{i+1}$ is the identity on $H$.

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary spherical fusion category over $\mathbb C$, with pivotal structure and spherical dimension as in [[def-pivotal-structure]], [[def-spherical-structure]], and [[def-the-dimension-of-an-object-relative-to-a-pivotal-structure]]. Let $a$ be a self-dual simple object with $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$. Choose a unit vector $v:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ spanning the one-dimensional vacuum split space and let $d_a>0$ be its positive spherical dimension.

A **normalized vacuum-channel self-duality datum** is a supplied pair of maps $\operatorname{coev}:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ and $\operatorname{ev}:a\otimes a\to\mathbf1$ of the form

$$\operatorname{coev}=\sqrt{d_a}\,v,\qquad \operatorname{ev}=\kappa_a\sqrt{d_a}\,v^\dagger,$$

where $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$ and the two duality zig-zag identities hold after the self-duality identification, using the left-dual convention of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]. We call $\kappa_a$ the **Frobenius–Schur sign in this normalized cup/cap convention**. It is not a braiding or $R$-symbol phase.

This item records supplied normalized duality data; it does not assert that every self-dual simple object admits the displayed gauge or prove a trace, ribbon, or category-equivalence theorem. An example must supply the datum or compute the sign from coherent normalized F-data; fusion rules alone do not specify it.

Let $a$ and $(v,\operatorname{ev},\operatorname{coev},d_a,\kappa_a)$ be as in [[def-anyonic-frobenius-schur-sign]]. In the multiplicity-free vacuum-normalized gauge of [[def-qc-tqc-f-symbol]],

$$\left(F^{aaa}_a\right)_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}=\frac{\kappa_a}{d_a},\qquad \delta_a:=\frac{1}{\left((F^{aaa}_a)^{-1}\right)_{\mathbf1,\mathbf1}}=\kappa_a d_a.$$

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary spherical fusion category over $\mathbb C$. Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects, with $a$ self-dual, $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$, and supply the normalized vacuum-channel self-duality datum with sign $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$ and positive spherical dimension $d_a$. For $n\ge3$, take the fixed-boundary repeated-$a$ path space $H_{a,n;b,c}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,T_n)$ with $T_0=b$ and $T_{j+1}=T_j\otimes a$, as in [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. Let $P_i=P_{i,\mathbf1}$ be the orthogonal local vacuum-channel projectors and put $U_i=\delta_aP_i$, where $\delta_a=\kappa_ad_a$. Then, for every $1\le i\le n-2$,

$$U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=U_{i+1}.$$

This supplies the reverse adjacent relation for the repeated-charge Temperley–Lieb family.

Let $n\ge2$, let $V$ be a complex vector space, and let $U_1,\ldots,U_{n-1}\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$. Suppose $\delta\in\mathbb C$, $q\in\mathbb C^\times$, and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, and assume

$$U_i^2=\delta U_i,\qquad U_iU_{i+1}U_i=U_i,\qquad U_{i+1}U_iU_{i+1}=U_{i+1}\quad(1\le i\le n-2),\qquad U_iU_j=U_jU_i\quad(|i-j|>1).$$

Define $B_i:=qI_V-U_i$. Then each $B_i$ is invertible with $B_i^{-1}=q^{-1}I_V-U_i$; the $B_i$ satisfy the Artin braid and far-commutation relations; and

$$(B_i-qI_V)(B_i+q^{-1}I_V)=0.$$

Thus $\sigma_i\mapsto B_i$ defines a group homomorphism $B_n\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$. If $H_v(n)$ is the generic type-A Hecke algebra with $(T_i-v)(T_i+1)=0$, its scalar specialization $H_{q^2}(n)$ has a unital algebra representation $T_i\mapsto qB_i$. This is the standard Hecke normalization because $(qB_i-q^2I_V)(qB_i+I_V)=0$. If $V$ is a complex Hilbert space and each $U_i$ is bounded self-adjoint, then $\delta\in\mathbb R$ and $|q|=1$ imply that each $B_i$ is unitary. No faithfulness, diagonalizability, or physical realization is asserted.

derivations.claim: If $v\in\operatorname{ran}P_i$, then $P_iv=v$ and $B_iv=(qI_V-\delta_aP_i)v=(q-\delta_a)v=-q^{-1}v$, using $q+q^{-1}=\delta_a$.

If $v\in\ker P_i$, then $P_iv=0$ and $B_iv=qv$. Since $P_i$ is an orthogonal projection by [F2], $V=\operatorname{ran}P_i\oplus\ker P_i$ orthogonally, so these two subspaces exhaust the operator's action and no absent subspace contributes an eigenvalue.

The source relation [F5] and local reverse relation [F6] supply all Temperley–Lieb hypotheses for [F7], with signed $\delta_a$ from [F4]. Thus the scalar actions above are the exchange eigenvalues on their respective channel subspaces; no physical transport or measurement premise is used.
